source_quote: Glucosamine-based nutraceuticals showed variable analgesic efficacy in canine osteoarthritis across systematic review and meta-analysis.
EPA and DHA omega-3 fatty acid supplementation was strongly associated with reduced inflammatory cytokine expression in canine joint disease.
Sulfur-containing joint support compounds improved owner-reported comfort outcomes in chronic canine musculoskeletal pain cohorts.
Zinc-dependent epidermal pathways contributed to improved barrier recovery markers in canine inflammatory skin disease.
Natural oral biofilm-active compounds reduced dental plaque accumulation over multi-week canine dental care protocols.
Taurine sufficiency correlated with improved echocardiographic and functional indicators in canine dilated cardiomyopathy.
Multi-strain probiotic administration lowered frequency of loose stool episodes and supported intestinal barrier integrity in dogs.
L-carnitine supplementation enhanced fat oxidation and preserved lean mass in canine calorie-restriction weight management programs.
Lutein-containing antioxidant supplementation reduced oxidative lens stress biomarkers in senile canine cataract patients.
Chondroitin sulfate was associated with improved cartilage resilience indicators in canine osteoarthritis nutraceutical meta-analysis.
